title: Define customer-facing model release note taxonomy + required sections per change type
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Context
We are standardizing model/version metadata and auto-generating customer-visible model release notes (“model changelog”). Today, updates are inconsistent across docs/Slack/runtime notes. Customers have asked for clearer release notes to support pinning, rollouts/A-B tests, and enterprise change-management.

This issue defines:
1) The taxonomy of customer-visible change types (labels) for model release notes.
2) The required sections per change type, so the generator can produce consistent, customer-safe notes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

## Goals
- A small, understandable set of customer-facing change types (not internal implementation categories).
- Generator-friendly requirements: each type maps to required/optional sections and minimal structured fields.
- Works for both “model version added” and “existing version updated metadata/compatibility/deprecation.”
- Align with Docs style constraints (no internal nicknames/vendor specifics; avoid leaking infra details).

## Non-goals
- Auto-generated narrative from eval diffs (v1 will link to metrics/dashboards only).
- Per-customer customized notes (same published note for all customers; account-tier gating handled elsewhere).

---

## Proposal: Release note taxonomy (customer-visible)
Release notes can carry 1+ change type labels. Use a primary type for template selection; additional labels appear as chips/tags in Console and feed.

### A) Bugfix
**Definition:** Fixes that address incorrect behavior vs documented/expected behavior, without intentionally changing model semantics beyond the fix.
**Examples:**
- Fix incorrect tool/function calling JSON schema emission (previously invalid JSON in edge cases).
- Fix tokenization/config mismatch causing truncation behavior inconsistent with documented context window.

### B) Performance
**Definition:** Changes intended to improve latency/throughput/cost characteristics for serving a model version. May include runtime/kernel/batching changes *only as customer-safe impact*.
**Examples:**
- Reduced time-to-first-token for streaming.
- Increased max stable TPS per replica for a specific model in Hosted.

### C) Compatibility
**Definition:** Adds/removes/changes compatibility with Redwood API features, deployment modes, regions, or integrations. Includes behavior changes in request/response contract.
**Examples:**
- Adds structured output support.
- Adds tool/function calling support.
- Changes default max_output_tokens cap.
- Adds availability in Private (on-prem package) or Dedicated.

### D) Deprecation
**Definition:** Any announcement of end-of-support/end-of-availability, sunset timeline, or recommended replacement.
**Examples:**
- Version is being sunset; after date X requests will fail unless migrated.
- Model is removed from default catalog but remains callable if pinned until date X.

### (Optional future label; NOT in MVP templates)
Safety/Policy: PM+Security agreed we may need a distinct label later for policy-driven changes; for v1, treat as Compatibility + required “Policy notes” section when present. (See “Policy notes” section requirement below.)

---

## Required sections (by change type)
All release notes share a consistent skeleton. The generator should always emit the “Universal” sections, and then include additional required sections depending on primary change type.

### Universal sections (ALWAYS REQUIRED)
1) **Summary** (2–4 sentences, customer-safe, no internal-only details)
2) **What changed** (bulleted list; factual; avoid speculation)
3) **Customer impact** (one of: none / low / medium / high; plus plain-language explanation)
4) **Applies to** (Hosted / Dedicated / Private; include region(s) if not global)
5) **Availability / rollout**
   - One of: available now | rolling out | scheduled
   - If rolling out: include window and how to pin to avoid surprises
6) **Version identifiers**
   - model_id, version_id (customer-visible IDs)
   - If this is an update to an existing version: include “effective_at” timestamp
7) **Links**
   - Console model page
   - Changelog entry permalink
   - Optional: eval/benchmark dashboard link(s) (no internal run IDs)

### Bugfix (additional REQUIRED)
- **Symptoms / who was affected** (customer-observable description, no internal incident references)
- **Workaround** (required if impact is medium/high and workaround exists; otherwise say “No workaround required.”)
- **Verification** (simple guidance: how to confirm behavior is resolved; can be as simple as “re-run request” + note on pinning)

### Performance (additional REQUIRED)
- **Expected performance impact**
  - Provide either: (a) relative directionality (improved/reduced) + metric names, or (b) approximate percent range if approved.
  - Metrics allowed: p50/p95 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, error rate.
  - Must include a disclaimer that performance varies by prompt length/concurrency/region.
- **No change to model outputs** statement (required unless outputs may change; if outputs may change, route to Compatibility and state so clearly)

### Compatibility (additional REQUIRED)
- **Compatibility notes** (explicitly list what features/modes are supported, and any constraints)
  - tool/function calling support
  - structured output support
  - context window / max_output_tokens constraints
  - deployment availability (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- **Action required**
  - One of: none | recommended | required
  - If required: list steps (e.g., update request schema, re-pin version)

### Deprecation (additional REQUIRED)
- **Deprecation timeline**
  - announce_date, sunset_date
  - behavior after sunset (fail, redirect to replacement, or continue only if allowlisted)
- **Replacement / migration path**
  - replacement model_id/version_id (or “TBD” if unknown, but then require follow-up date)
  - migration guidance (API changes, expected differences)
- **Support policy**
  - what support looks like during deprecation window
  - who to contact for exceptions (enterprise)

### Policy notes (conditionally REQUIRED)
If metadata indicates policy/safety related changes (internal flag from schema; visible text must be customer-safe):
- **Policy notes** (customer-safe; must not include internal vendor policy names, internal thresholds, or enforcement tooling)

---

## Console + Feed display rules
- Each entry has: primary_type + additional_labels.
- Filters: by type label, date, model_id, deployment availability.
- For “rolling out” entries, Console should show pinned version guidance and link to rollouts history.

---

## Generator/template requirements (implementation notes)
- Primary change type chooses the template and required sections.
- Generator should error (draft remains blocked) if required structured fields are missing for the chosen primary type (e.g., Deprecation missing sunset_date).
- Allow “multi-label” but enforce a single primary type for template selection.
- Keep Summary under ~500 chars; What changed bullets under ~6 items.

---

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Taxonomy agreed by PM + Docs lead + Release Eng lead.
- [x] Required sections enumerated per change type and mapped to generator behavior.
- [x] Explicit rules for performance claims and customer-safe language.
- [x] Policy notes requirement clarified for v1.
- [x] Follow-up created for template linting and CI enforcement in docs (handled in engineering/docs workstreams).

## Open questions / follow-ups
1) Do we expose “Safety/Policy” as a customer-visible label in v1?
   - Decision: not in v1 taxonomy. Use Compatibility + “Policy notes” section when present.
2) Can we include numeric perf deltas in v1?
   - Decision: allowed but requires PM + Release Eng approval during review; otherwise use directional language + metric names.

2026-01-30 — Paula Mendes: Added multi-label approach (primary + tags) so Console filtering stays flexible without exploding templates. Will coordinate with ENG-4926 on enforcement behavior (blocking drafts when required fields missing).
